K-12 Funding — Inclusive Education (Province of British Columbia)
CMEC / Government of Canada, Protocol for Agreements for Minority-Language Education and Second-Language Instruction, 2024-2025 to 2027-2028 (signed)
Official Languages Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 31 (4th Supp.)), s. 43 - Special mandate of Minister of Canadian Heritage
CMEC / Government of Canada, Protocol 2019-2020 to 2022-2023
Constitution Act 1867, s. 93 (Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada)

existing_terminology:
There is no federal category, because there is no federal school system
Each province names and codes language difficulty its own way
Ontario codes 'Language Impairment', Alberta codes by severity, BC codes nothing
Education is exclusively provincial under s. 93 of the Constitution Act 1867
existing_identificationCriteria: Not established from the sources consulted. Section 93 of the Constitution Act 1867 gives each provincial legislature the exclusive power to make laws in relation to education, so there is no federal body that identifies a language disorder and no national criteria to record. What exists is thirteen separate provincial and territorial answers.
existing_serviceModel:
No pan-Canadian model exists; British Columbia is given here as the documented example
BC funds speech-language pathology out of the Basic Allocation, not a supplemental category
BC's eight supplemental Inclusive Education categories have no speech or language one
Supplemental funding requires assessment, identification and a current IEP
existing_legalEntitlement:
No national entitlement exists to compare
Entitlement is provincial, and the provinces do not converge
A child moving between provinces can change category, funding and service model
existing_funding:
BC Basic Allocation is a standard per-student amount for each school-age student enrolled
BC boards reporting one of three levels get supplemental Inclusive Education funding on top
Those supplemental funds are not targeted to specific students, but go to the board

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Guatemala: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
The 1991 education law art. 47 reaches language obliquely (PEER rendering in English)
It covers disabilities 'in their linguistic, intellectual or physical' development
The 2007 law defines needs by curricular disadvantage, not by named condition
existing_identificationCriteria:
2007 special education law: disadvantage and difficulty benefiting from the age group curriculum
Special school placement where needs prevent successful integration into mainstream schools
existing_multilingualProvision:
The 1996 law requires bilingual education in majority-indigenous areas
That duty applies to programmes for pupils with disabilities in rural areas
It is the only explicit multilingual clause found in Guatemalan SEN law
existing_serviceModel:
Resource centres for inclusive education have been rolled out since 2019
The Dirección General de Educación Especial runs them
existing_legalEntitlement: The 1996 disability law gives mainstream access with required support services
existing_funding:
The Educational Inclusion Project is funded by the International Bureau of Education (PEER)
Departmental coordinators also help obtain scholarships for students with disabilities
existing_workforce:
The General Directorate of Special Education has a coordinator in each of the 22 departments
Special education centres in municipalities have trained interdisciplinary teams (PEER)
Departmental special education coordinators give technical help to mainstream teachers (PEER)

docLinks.label: Diario Oficial de la Federación, ediciones en PDF

existing_terminology:
The law works from 'barreras para el aprendizaje y la participación'
Barriers to learning and participation, not from a list of conditions
No statutory category corresponds to DLD
Educación especial is defined by what it removes, not by whom it is for
existing_identificationCriteria:
Ley General de Educación art. 64
Special education is provided on the decision and prior assessment of the learner
Together with parents or guardians and teaching staff
And where applicable on referral arising from a health condition
existing_multilingualProvision:
The state guarantees linguistic rights to indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples, LGE art. 56
Indigenous education must answer needs with cultural and linguistic pertinence
Materials, free textbooks included, must be made in the country's various languages
existing_serviceModel:
Centros de Atención Múltiple are a recognised school type in their own right
Accessible formats are required, wherever possible inside mainstream services
That does not cancel the option of a school-based placement
existing_legalEntitlement:
Art. 64(IV): the state must establish a system of early diagnosis
And specialised attention, to remove barriers to learning and participation
Art. 64(V): all teaching staff must be trained to identify and remove those barriers
Educación especial must be available across every type, level and modality
existing_funding:
Federal executive and each state jointly finance public education, LGE art. 119
Annual public education spending may not fall below 8 per cent of GDP
existing_workforce:
Federal authority sets accreditation and certification rules for special education staff
Teachers are to be posted to the linguistic regions they themselves belong to

docLinks.label: Ley No. 582, Ley General de Educación (Nicaragua, 2006) — full text as published by FAOLEX from the Asamblea Nacional's Normaweb record
UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Nicaragua: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
Terms in Ley 582 are 'personas con habilidades diferentes' and special educational needs
Ley 582 does not name language or speech disorder anywhere
The only communication-specific provision in the law is sign language
existing_identificationCriteria: Educacion Basica Especial is for those whose disability hinders regular learning
existing_serviceModel:
Inclusion in regular classrooms, with complementary personalised attention allowed
25 public special education schools nationally, per the ministry via PEER
Eight diversity resource centres sit inside teacher training colleges
existing_legalEntitlement:
Ley 582 binds public and private schools to include pupils with disabilities
The duty is framed as programme design, not an individual therapy entitlement
existing_funding:
Ley 582 art. 88: the state guarantees each public school its running-cost budget line
Art. 90 bans fees, voluntary quotas or any other payment in state primary and secondary
A school community may still organise economic activities for the school's benefit
Art. 92: the state must fight any economic barrier limiting education
existing_workforce:
Teacher training must include study of Nicaraguan Sign Language
No speech and language therapist role appears in Ley 582

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Panama: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
SEN, in PEER's English rendering; the Spanish originals were not retrieved
The 2006 inclusive education plan defines SEN by difficulty progressing
No language, speech or communication category is named in the instruments read
existing_identificationCriteria:
In PEER's English: SEN assessment is the interdisciplinary team's responsibility
The team is external to the school: psychologists, social workers and teachers
existing_multilingualProvision:
Act 88 of 2010 recognizes indigenous languages and alphabets and regulates bilingual education
MEDUCA must regulate indigenous language use in schools in the comarcas and collective lands
The stated aim is to preserve the native language and promote Spanish and English
existing_serviceModel:
Educational support services operate across thirteen educational regions
The support is described as temporary, advising on plans and proposals
existing_legalEntitlement:
Act 42 of 27 August 1999 requires inclusion with support services and technical aids
Executive Decree No. 1 of 4 February 2000 regulates placement
Priority is given to the mainstream centre nearest the pupil's home
existing_funding: State must allocate funds where family resources are insufficient or access is difficult
existing_workforce:
The support-service staffing list contains no speech and language therapist
It names special education, psychology, social work and learning difficulties

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, Paraguay — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)
Paraguay, Ley N° 1264/1998 General de Educación, full text (Cap. IV, Arts. 80–84; Art. 31; Art. 75)

existing_terminology:
Ley 1264/1998 Art. 80 names trastornos de lenguaje as a statutory SEN category
It sits alongside superdotados, dificultades de aprendizaje, trastornos de conducta
The later Ley 5136/2013 drops the term for necesidades especificas de apoyo
The 2013 list names specific learning disorders but not language disorder
existing_identificationCriteria:
Art. 31 requires early-years prevention and early-detection assessment
That duty names intellectual level and sensory impairment, not language
Art. 84 makes early diagnosis and treatment an explicit government duty
existing_multilingualProvision:
Art. 31: teaching is in the pupil's official mother tongue from first grade
The other official language is taught from the start as a second language
Guarani and Spanish are both official and the rule is symmetrical between them
existing_serviceModel:
Around 70 special schools and centres existed in 2014
Inclusion support centres replace special schools under the 2018-2023 plan
Special-education content and assessment are approved by the MEC under Art. 82
Eradicating special schools is a stated goal of the inclusive education directorate
existing_legalEntitlement:
Art. 80 obliges the state to guarantee formacion basica for the named groups
Art. 81 requires integrated placement in mainstream schools where possible
Ley 5136/2013 extends the duty to public, private and subsidised institutions
existing_funding:
Admission to free public institutions must be eased for people of limited means
Where public places are absent or too few, the state buys private places by grant
FONACIDE has financed school repairs and adaptations, textbooks, ICT and teacher training
existing_workforce:
Art. 83 requires specialised training for teachers in this modality
No fonoaudiologo or terapeuta del lenguaje is named in the statute, term count 0

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Honduras: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
SEN, in PEER's English rendering; the Spanish originals were not retrieved
The 2014 resolution: difficulties of varying severity, 'not necessarily due to disability'
No language, speech or communication category is named in the instruments read
existing_identificationCriteria:
Resolution 1365 of 2014 creates a departmental psychopedagogical support team
In PEER's English, that team identifies pupils' needs via diagnostic assessments
existing_serviceModel:
Special education centres support mainstream schools through itinerant teams
The 2014 resolution converts special centres into inclusion resource centres
existing_legalEntitlement:
The 2005 disability equity act guarantees access at all education levels
In both the public and the private systems
existing_workforce: No speech and language therapist role was found in any instrument read
